newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Losses to Slovnaft shares pull Slovak BSE down.
newsitem.headline: Losses to Slovnaft shares pull Slovak BSE down.

text.p: Slovak blue chips were mixed in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with losses to shares of oil refiner Slovnaft helping pull the SAX index down 1.44 points to 185.98.
Slovnaft, the most capitalised issue on BSE, closed down 25 crowns at 780, and said they expected a further decline in the issue as there has been no significant orders seen on the bourse.
"It is virtually impossible to buy or sell in Slovnaft at the moment," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
On the contrary, Sykora said he expected steel maker VSZ, the next largest issue on the bourse, to rise, though the share has recently failed to trade in larger volumes.
"I think it has a potential of growth, maybe up to some 660 crown level," he said.
VSZ closed up two crowns at 642, but only 204 shares traded on the BSE floor.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta did not trade on Monday, hwile the country's largest commercial bank VUB closed unchanged at 1,680 crowns.
Overall volume, boosted mainly by direct trades, rose to 517,630 shares, from 360,883 shares traded on Friday, while turnover increased to 392.48 million crowns, from 279.23 million.
